title: U.S. Copyright Office finding on unauthorized digital replicas of voice and likeness
system_purpose: Consumer and professional AI tools that clone a person's voice or visual likeness from a sample so that new speech or performance can be synthesised on demand.
decision_impact: Determines whether a performer's voice or likeness is reused in commercial content, and whether they are asked, credited or paid for that reuse.
affected_groups: voice actors and performers;musicians;public figures;private individuals whose recordings are publicly available;creators who license replicas
verified_facts: The Copyright Office examined unauthorized digital replicas and concluded that the current mix of state right-of-publicity laws and federal law is an inadequate and inconsistent remedy, and it recommended new federal digital replica protection. Part 1 of the report was published on 31 July 2024. The Office states that its August 2023 notice of inquiry received over 10,000 comments by December 2023.
reported_harm: Stakeholders reported loss of control over their own voice and likeness, unpaid commercial substitution of their performances, reputational damage from words they never said, and enforcement costs falling on the individual rather than the tool provider.
quantitative_evidence: Over 10,000 comments received between August 2023 and December 2023 in response to one notice of inquiry covering AI generally, not digital replicas alone. The Office published no incidence count of unauthorized replicas, so no rate of harm can be derived from this source and the comment total is not a denominator for anything.
limitations: This is a policy recommendation, not a judicial finding of liability, and the reported comment volume measures stakeholder concern rather than the frequency or severity of actual replica incidents. Scope is United States law only.

title: FTC enforcement action against an AI writing service over a testimonial and review generator
system_purpose: A subscription generative AI writing tool with a template that produced testimonial and product-review copy from a short prompt for creators and marketers to publish.
decision_impact: Shapes what review and endorsement copy a creator publishes to an audience that treats it as first-hand experience, which in turn drives purchase decisions.
affected_groups: consumers reading published reviews;honest reviewers and creators;competing sellers;platform operators hosting the reviews
verified_facts: The FTC brought an administrative action alleging the service's review feature could generate detailed reviews containing specific claims the subscriber had never supplied, and that the provider furnished the means to produce deceptive content. The docket also records that the 2024 final order was set aside in 2025, so the matter did not end in a standing order.
reported_harm: Alleged consumer deception through fabricated first-hand experience, dilution of the value of genuine reviews, and unfair disadvantage to creators who only publish what they have actually tested.
quantitative_evidence: No verified count of deceptive reviews published or consumers affected is available in the docket; the FTC characterised the feature as capable of generating detailed reviews at scale for paying subscribers, and the only firm procedural figure is that the final order was set aside in 2025.
limitations: The allegations were never proven on the merits and the final order was vacated, so this case supports a foreseeable-hazard and regulatory-exposure claim, not a finding that the tool caused measured consumer harm.

title: FCC enforcement against AI-cloned voice impersonation of a real identifiable person
system_purpose: Voice-cloning generation used to synthesise speech in the voice of a real, identifiable public figure, then distributed as automated audio to a mass audience.
decision_impact: Determines whether recipients believe a real named person said something they never said, at a moment when that belief changes their behaviour.
affected_groups: the impersonated individual;recipients of the synthetic audio;the wider public;voice-cloning tool providers
verified_facts: On 8 February 2024 the FCC ruled that an AI-generated voice is an artificial voice under existing US telephone consumer protection rules. It then proposed a six million US dollar forfeiture in May 2024 and issued the Forfeiture Order in September 2024 against the individual responsible for automated calls that used an AI-cloned voice of a real identifiable public figure to discourage voting in a primary election.
reported_harm: Impersonation of a real person without consent, manipulation of recipients through a trusted familiar voice, and reputational harm to the person whose voice was cloned.
quantitative_evidence: A six million US dollar forfeiture, proposed May 2024 and issued September 2024, against one individual. The number of recipients actually deceived is not quantified in the order, so exposure cannot be inferred from the penalty.
limitations: This is a telecom and election-integrity enforcement action, not a creator-platform incident, so it transfers to this product only as evidence of the impersonation capability and the regulatory response to it, not as evidence about creator workflows or platform incidence rates.
